name: landbot
description: Build and publish AI conversion agents in Landbot from ChatGPT or Codex: qualify website visitors, book meetings and route leads, on your site and on WhatsApp.

interface.longDescription:
Build AI agents and chatbots for your website and WhatsApp that qualify leads, book meetings and answer customer questions — by describing what you need in this chat. Landbot runs the agent; ChatGPT builds it in your Landbot account.

What you can do
- Qualify visitors — ask the questions your sales team would, and route by the answers.
- Book meetings — offer qualified visitors a Calendly slot inside the conversation.
- Capture and route leads — send answers to your Google Sheet or email.
- Answer from your own content — point the agent at your website or documents.
- Answer support questions — resolve FAQs from your own content and hand off to your team.
- Launch on WhatsApp — the same agent, on the channel your customers already use.
- Test, then go live — try it on a test link; it’s published only when you say so.

Who it’s for
Marketing, sales and support teams that run conversations on their website or WhatsApp and want leads qualified and customer questions answered.

Before you start
- You need a Landbot account. You sign in with Landbot when you connect.
- Nothing goes live without your confirmation: agents are built as drafts, tested on a link and published only when you approve.
- WhatsApp agents need a WhatsApp number connected in Landbot first.
- Google Sheets, email and Calendly steps use accounts you connect in Landbot.

Security
Landbot is SOC 2 and GDPR compliant. Security documentation, DPA and subprocessor list at trust.landbot.io.
capabilities: Create web and WhatsApp bots from a plain-language description
Read Landbot's live block catalog and wire blocks into a working flow
Edit the flow of an existing bot: messages, questions, buttons and connections
Create AI agents that answer from your texts and web pages
Connect Google Sheets, SendGrid and Calendly blocks to your brand's accounts
Style the web chat with Custom CSS, a header title and avatar, and the texts visitors see
Deploy a bot to test, and publish it once you approve
defaultPrompt: Build a conversion agent for my pricing page that qualifies visitors and shares my demo booking link with the good ones.
Build a support chatbot for my website that answers FAQs from my help center and hands tricky cases to my team.
Add an AI agent to my homepage that answers buying questions from my website and collects emails from interested visitors.

positive.description: Reads the FAQ an AI agent answers from, without changing anything. The test account has a web bot named Demo FAQ agent whose AI agent has a knowledge source with its FAQ turned on.
positive.prompt: In my Demo FAQ agent bot, show me the questions and answers its AI agent answers from.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Demo FAQ agent bot, reads its draft to find its AI agent, and lists the agent's knowledge sources and the FAQ answers generated from them, each with the questions it answers. If it first asks to confirm the bot, the user says yes. It changes nothing.

positive.description: Builds a new web bot from a plain-language description, without publishing it.
positive.prompt: Create a web chatbot called Newsletter signup that asks for the visitor's name and email, then thanks them.
positive.tools_triggered: get_guide, list_blocks, get_block_definition, create_bot, update_web_chat, add_draft_blocks
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the build guide and the block catalog, creates a web bot named Newsletter signup, switches its chat to the v4 web chat, and adds a greeting, a name question, an email question and a thank-you message, connected in that order. It hands the bot back with its builder link and a plain description of the conversation, says whether the draft breaks any rule, and offers to let the user try it or publish it, without doing either until the user says yes.

positive.description: Changes a message in the draft of a bot the account already has. The test account has a web bot named Demo lead form.
positive.prompt: In my Demo lead form bot, change the last message to: Thanks! We'll get back to you within one business day.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Demo lead form bot, reads its draft and changes the text of its final message. If it first asks to confirm the bot, the user says yes. It says the change is in the draft and reaches visitors only when the bot is published.

positive.description: Deploys a bot's draft to its test copy once the user has asked for it.
positive.prompt: Deploy my Demo lead form bot to its test link in Landbot so I can try it before publishing.
positive.expected_behavior: Deploys the Demo lead form draft to the bot's test copy, reports any warnings, and tells the user to open the bot's test link in Landbot to try it. Visitors keep getting the published version, and nothing is published.

positive.description: Styles a web bot's chat with Custom CSS.
positive.prompt: Give the chat of my Demo lead form bot a dark background and orange buttons.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads how the chat looks, the style guide and what Custom CSS can style, and writes Custom CSS with a dark background and orange buttons. If it first asks to confirm the bot, the user says yes. It says whether the change went live or went to the chat's draft, which visitors get the next time the bot is published.

negative.description: A general question unrelated to Landbot. No Landbot tool should run; ChatGPT answers on its own.
A web page, not a conversation. The plugin should not create a bot or call any Landbot tool; ChatGPT can help with the HTML itself.
negative.prompt: Write the HTML for a landing page for my bakery.

negative.description: Messaging people is outside the plugin: it builds bots and has no tool that sends messages to contacts. It should call no Landbot tool and say it cannot send the message.
negative.prompt: Send a WhatsApp message to all my customers saying we're closed tomorrow.

publication.release_notes: First release: build, edit, style, test and publish Landbot bots and AI agents from ChatGPT and Codex through the Landbot MCP server, including managing an AI agent's FAQ and getting the link and the embed code of a published web bot.
